our_worker.diagnosis: NOT the platform and NOT the volume: the vendor control above completed on the same volume, the same datacenter and the same GPU class. The container never produced a single log line, so the failure is before serve_handler.py's first print — the SDK banner '--- Starting Serverless Worker ---' that the pod proof emitted never appeared. The serverless job-loop path (runpod.serverless.start with no --rp_serve_api) has NEVER executed in this project: 5b aborted before any worker ran, and srv-2a's pod proof exercised the HTTP-server mode of the same file. The suspect is therefore the one thing the pod proof cannot cover — whether `--docker-start-cmd bash,/runpod-volume/start.sh` actually becomes the worker's main process under the stock runpod/pytorch image, whose own entrypoint may take precedence. UNPROVEN: no log line exists to confirm it.
our_worker.the_rungs_own_explanation_was_wrong: the runbook's handshake-timeout row attributes the trigger to 'the weights are not where HF_HOME says'. They were: the pod loaded them off this same volume minutes earlier, and the container emitted zero lines so it never reached a load at all. The trigger condition was right and its attributed cause was not. A next runbook's row should read 'the container may not be starting at all — run the vendor control first'.

spend.anchor: results/spend_srv2b.json, written before the first billable action
spend.breakdown_note: staging pod ~$0.37 (billing pods reports $0.29799634497612715 over 1441266 ms) and ~$0.55 of serverless worker time that consumed no job — a crash-looping worker bills at the flex rate exactly like a working one.
spend.guard_billing_blind_spot: runpod_guard's corroborating reading walks `billing pods` and `billing network-volume` only. The serverless worker's ~$0.55 appears in neither, so the guard printed $18.6344 of billing against a $19.4987 balance delta — an $0.86 under-count. On a serverless step only the balance delta binds, which is why `spend()` takes the max of the two. Worth knowing when the cap is $4.00 and a crash-looping worker can eat 14% of it without showing up in the check SPEC 3.4 (4) names.
